1. When the clinic asks `"Which appointment would you like to move?"`, [DriverHearing](file:///work/clinicbench/hearing.py#L60-L61) extracts `questions: ["target_appt"]`.
2. In [PatientPolicy.answer](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L112-L117), when `prop == "target_appt"` and the patient has no `target_appt` (e.g., a booking-only patient), `true_values("target_appt")` returns `([], [])`, so `answer` returns `([], [{"k": "prop", "name": "target_appt", "aff": []}])`. Because `qs` is non-empty, [PatientPolicy.respond](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L469-L470) sets `act = "answer"` instead of falling back to `ask`/`insist`. Fixed the empty-reply bug in [policy.py](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py) and [voice.py](file:///work/clinicbench/voice.py):

- **[PatientPolicy.answer](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L112-L171)**: Avoid emitting empty `prop` parts (and empty proposition entries) when `target_appt` has no value in truth or when another proposition (`slot`, `doctor`, etc.) has no affirmed/excluded values in the current mode (`unlocked`, `clear`, `hedged`, or `contradictory`).
- **[PatientPolicy.respond](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L472-L485)**: Track `q_ents` and `q_parts` produced by `qs` so `act` is only set to `'answer'` / `'cant_say'` (and `_pressure_parts` added there) when `q_parts` is non-empty; otherwise `act` remains `None` and falls through to `'ask'` / `'insist'`.
- **[Voice.say](file:///work/clinicbench/voice.py#L251-L257)**: Fall back to a non-empty `ask` line if `dedup` is empty, ensuring `Voice.say` never returns a blank reply.

The blank patient reply is caused by a bug in the frozen instrument code (`PatientPolicy` and `Voice`), not in the driver.

When a patient who only came in to book (`truth["target_appt"]` is `None`) is asked `"Which appointment would you like to move?"`:
1. [hearing.py](file:///work/clinicbench/hearing.py#L60-L61) (`DriverHearing.__call__`) extracts `questions: ["target_appt"]`.
2. [policy.py](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L115-L117) (`PatientPolicy.answer`) gets `aff = []` from `true_values("target_appt")` and returns `[], [{"k": "prop", "name": "target_appt", "aff": []}]`.
3. [policy.py](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L462-L470) (`PatientPolicy.respond`) sets `act = "answer"` because `qs` is non-empty, without falling back to `request` or `ask`.
4. [voice.py](file:///work/clinicbench/voice.py#L112-L136) (`Voice._prop`) returns `""` when both `aff` and `exc` are empty, and [voice.py](file:///work/clinicbench/voice.py#L189-L192) (`Voice.say`) skips empty strings, producing a blank reply.

Because `clinicbench/policy.py` and `clinicbench/voice.py` are listed in [phase3-freeze.json](file:///work/docs/phase3-freeze.json#L10-L11), this is a `fix`.

Fixed the blank-reply bug when a patient without a `target_appt` (e.g., book-only) is asked a `target_appt` question:

- **[clinicbench/policy.py](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L115-L119)**: In `PatientPolicy.answer`, return `[], []` instead of emitting a `prop` part with `aff=[]` when `target_appt` has no value.
- **[clinicbench/policy.py](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L442-L450)**: In `PatientPolicy.respond`, handle `"target_appt"` in `qs` when `not self.t["target_appt"]` the same way as `"intent"`—remove it from `qs`, append a `"request"` part so the patient restates their request, and set `act = act or "ask"`.
- **[clinicbench/voice.py](file:///work/clinicbench/voice.py#L251-L257)**: In `Voice.say`, fall back to a standard `"ask"` prompt if `dedup` is empty so `Voice.say` never returns a blank line.

### Verification
- `python -m clinicbench.selftest` passed (`SELFTEST PASS`: 57/57 golden, 556/556 mutation, 10368/10368 stub grid, 3456/3456 adapter).
- Verified directly with a book-only patient asked `"Which appointment would you like to move?"` via `DriverHearing`: `PatientPolicy.respond` returned `act="ask"` with `propositions=[]`, `Voice.say` restated the booking request, `PatientPolicy.answer("target_appt")` returned `([], [])`, and `Voice.say` with an empty `target_appt` prop returned a non-empty fallback line.
